}} '''Ibou Dianko Badji''' (born 13 October 2002) is a Senegalese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Shenzhen Leopards]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). ==Early life and career== In 2017–18, Badji trained with [[NBA Academy Africa]] in [[Saly]], [[Senegal]], where he emerged as one of the best prospects in his age group.{{cite web |title=El Barça ficha al 'rey del mate' senegalés de 16 años y 2,18 |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/baloncesto-barca/barca-ficha-rey-del-mate-senegales-anos-218-7221612 |website=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]] |access-date=29 March 2020 |language=Spanish |date=27 December 2018}} By the time he turned 15 years old, he stood about {{height|m=2.16}} with a {{height|m=2.29}} [[wingspan]].{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Inside the NBA Academy and what it means for future prospects |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21894042/inside-nba-academy-africa-means-future-basketball |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=29 March 2020 |date=28 December 2017}} On 27 December 2018, Badji signed with Spanish basketball club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] and began playing for its youth sections.{{cite web |title=El Barcelona ata al 'anti-Tavares' del futuro forjado por la NBA: 16 años y 2,16 metros |url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2018/12/28/5c265025e2704e854a8b4605.html |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |access-date=29 March 2020 |language=Spanish |date=28 December 2018}} In December 2019, he played for U18 FC Barcelona at [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Valencia, Spain|ANGT Valencia]], where he averaged eight points, 8.8 rebounds and five blocks per game.{{cite web |last1=Domínguez |first1=Juan |title=Primera jornada del ANGT de Valencia: Roko Prkacin, Alonso Faure… |url=https://fullbasket.es/2019/12/27/primera-jornada-del-adidas-next-generation-tournament-roko-prkacin-alonso-faure/ |website=Fullbasket |access-date=29 March 2020 |language=Spanish |date=27 December 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Barcelona (2019–2021)=== To prepare for the 2019–20 season, Badji trained with the [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|first team]] of Barcelona.{{cite web |title=Fc Barcelone : Le jeune Ibou Badji avec l'équipe première |url=https://www.lequotidien.sn/fc-barcelone-le-jeune-ibou-badji-avec-lequipe-premiere/ |website=[[Le Quotidien (Senegal)|Le Quotidien]] |access-date=29 March 2020 |language=French |date=29 August 2019}} He spent much of the season playing for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet B|FC Barcelona B]], the club's [[reserve team]], in the third-tier [[LEB Plata]]. On 26 October 2019, Badji had a season-high 12 points, nine rebounds and five blocks in an 86–77 win over [[CB Prat|Prat]].{{cite web |title=Espagne – LEB Plata : Brancou Badio et Ibou Badji décisifs avec le Barça |url=https://www.basketsenegal.com/2019/10/28/espagne-leb-plata-brancou-badio-et-ibou-badji-decisifs-avec-le-barca/ |website=Basketsenegal |access-date=29 March 2020 |language=French |date=28 October 2019}} On 18 January 2020, he recorded eight points and a season-high eight blocks in an 88–80 victory over Prat.{{cite web |title=8 tapones con el filial del Barça para Ibou Badji: te lo presentamos |url=https://www.gigantes.com/cantera/jovenes-promesas/ibou-badji-tapones-prat-barcelona/ |website=Gigantes del Basket |access-date=29 March 2020 |language=Spanish |date=18 January 2020}} ===Força Lleida (2021–2022)=== On 4 October 2021, Badji signed with [[Força Lleida CE]] of the [[LEB Oro]].{{cite web |title=Ibou Badji joins Lleida |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Spain/news/707549/Ibou-Badji-joins-Lleida |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October 5, 2021 |date=October 5, 2021}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], on 3 November 2022, Badji was named to the opening night roster for the [[Wisconsin Herd]] after signing an Exhibition 10 contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/wisconsin-herd-announces-2022-23-opening-day-roster/n-5895537|title=Wisconsin Herd Announces 2022-23 Opening Day Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} On 18 November 2022, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] announced that they had signed Badji to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Portland Trail Blazers Sign Ibou Badji to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-trail-blazers-sign-ibou-badji-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=November 18, 2022|access-date=November 18, 2022}} On 7 March 2023, he underwent surgery on his left knee and was ruled out for at least eight weeks, thus missing out on playing the rest of the season.{{cite web|title=IBOU BADJI INJURY UPDATE|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/ibou-badji-injury-update|website=NBA.com|date=7 March 2023|access-date=16 March 2023}} On 6 July 2023, Badji signed another two-way contract with the Trail Blazers,{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Ibou Badji And John Butler Jr. To Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-re-sign-ibou-badji-and-john-butler-jr-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2023|access-date=6 July 2023}} but was waived on 24 October.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Duop Reath to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-duop-reath-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=24 October 2023|access-date=29 October 2023}} Six days later, he returned to the Herd.{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCE 2023 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announce-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=30 October 2023|access-date=23 January 2024}}{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Owczarski|title=Drew Timme, Alex Antetokounmpo, Glenn Robinson III headline the Wisconsin Herd camp roster|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2023/10/30/wisconsin-herd-training-camp-roster-drew-timme-alex-antetokounmpo-glenn-robinson-iii/71382175007/|work=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|date=30 October 2023|access-date=1 November 2023}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023–2024)=== On 22 November 2023, Badji signed another [[two-way contract]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Ibou Badji To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-re-sign-ibou-badji-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=22 November 2023|access-date=23 November 2023}} On 26 December 2023, Badji made his NBA debut for the Trail Blazers in a 130–113 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]]{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings vs Portland Trail Blazers - Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401585041|website=ESPN.com|date=26 December 2023|access-date=23 January 2024}} and two days later, he put up 7 points, 9 rebounds, and 3 blocks in 14 minutes of action in a 118–105 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs vs Portland Trail Blazers - Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401585055|website=ESPN.com|date=28 December 2023|access-date=23 January 2024}} ===Return to Wisconsin (2024–2025)=== On 12 September 2024, Badji signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], but was waived the same day.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bucks Sign, Waive Ibou Badji|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/bucks-to-sign-ibou-badji.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=13 September 2024|access-date=13 September 2024}} On 28 October, he rejoined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2024-25 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=28 October 2024|access-date=29 October 2024}} ===La Laguna Tenerife (2025)=== On April 3, 2025, Badji signed with [[CB 1939 Canarias|La Laguna Tenerife]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://cbcanarias.net/2025/04/03/ibou-badji-nuevo-jugador-de-la-laguna-tenerife/|title=Ibou Badji, nuevo jugador de La Laguna Tenerife|last=|first=|date=April 3, 2025|website=cbcanarias.net|publisher=|language=En|access-date=April 3, 2025}} ===Greensboro Swarm (2025–2026)=== On September 30, 2025, Badji signed a training camp contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web |title=Hornets' Ibou Badji: Signs with Charlotte |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hornets-ibou-badji-signs-with-charlotte/|website=CBS Sports |publisher=RotoWire via CBS Sports |date=September 30, 2025 |access-date=October 9, 2025}} He appeared in one preseason game, recording two points and three rebounds in 11 minutes during a loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], before being waived by the Hornets on October 14, prior to the start of the regular season.{{cite web |title=Hornets Waive Center Ibou Badji |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/10/hornets-waive-center-ibou-badji.html|website=HoopsRumors |date=October 14, 2025 |access-date=October 14, 2025}} On November 6, 2025, Badji was named to the [[Greensboro Swarm]] opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-finalize-opening-night-roster-2|title=GREENSBORO SWARM FINALIZE OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 6, 2025|access-date=November 6, 2025}} ==National team career== Badji represented [[Senegal national under-19 basketball team|Senegal]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. He averaged 6.9 points, 5.1 rebounds and 3.1 blocks per game, which ranked second in the tournament, as his team finished in 15th place.{{cite web|title=Five players who blossomed at U19 World Cup|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2019/news/five-players-who-blossomed-at-u19-world-cup|work=[[FIBA]]|date=12 July 2019|access-date=29 March 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2023}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland]] | 22 || 1 || 10.3 || .636 || {{sort|-|—}} || .500 || 2.3 || .6 || .1 || .9 || 1.5 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 22 || 1 || 10.3 || .636 || — || .500 || 2.3 || .6 || .1 || .9 || 1.5 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * [https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Ibou-Badji/Summary/133690 RealGM.com profile] {{Senegal squad FIBA AfroBasket 2025}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Badji, Ibou}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century Senegalese sportsmen]] [[Category:Basketball players from Dakar]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:FC Barcelona Bàsquet B players]] [[Category:Força Lleida CE players]] [[Category:Greensboro Swarm players]] [[Category:Liga ACB players]] [[Category:NBA Academy Africa players]] [[Category:Portland Trail Blazers players]] [[Category:Rip City Remix players]] [[Category:Senegalese expatriate basketball people in Spain]] [[Category:Senegalese expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Senegalese men's basketball players]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:Windy City Bulls players]] [[Category:Wisconsin Herd players]]
